title: Aft Pylon Fairing Skin — Composite Scarf Repair for Heat and Impact Damage
abstract: Permanent scarf repair for heat degradation and impact damage in the aft pylon fairing skin, done off the aircraft on a spare fairing so that the cure cycle does not hold the aircraft.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the laminate strength of the aft pylon fairing skin after heat degradation or impact damage, and is written to be done on a removed fairing rather than in place.
sections.damage_assessment: Map the damage by tap test and confirm the extent by ultrasonic scan. Heat degradation shows as a colour change on the inner face before it shows any mechanical effect, so map the discoloured region as well and treat its full extent as suspect. Damage up to 90 mm across, in the skin only, not reaching a fastener line and not extending into a bonded edge member, is inside this repair. Damage above 90 mm, damage that reaches the lug attachment ROD165267-21 footprint, or any damage that has separated the skin from the doubler JAR270491-60, is outside it and the fairing is replaced. Record the fairing serial number and the number of previous repairs; a fairing with two existing scarf repairs is not repaired a third time.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the fairing to the applicable removal task and put it on the padded trestles with the damaged face up. Remove the damaged laminate by scarf sanding to the ratio on repair drawing RD-54-50-13-007, taking one ply per step and checking the ply count as you go. CAUTION: DO NOT SAND THROUGH INTO THE OPPOSITE FACE SHEET. Clean the scarf with the approved solvent and dry it. Lay up the replacement plies in the orientation sequence on the drawing, adding one overlap ply beyond the scarf edge. Cure under vacuum with the heat blanket at the temperature and time given. Do a tap test and an ultrasonic scan of the repaired area and of a 100 mm border around it. Where the heat shield standoff bosses fall inside the repair, re-establish the boss positions from the drawing before the fairing is closed. Restore the external finish and re-install the fairing skin panel D5450133608027 with countersunk screws EN962457-4D and washers AES161398-12.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is not life limited but requires a tap test of the repaired area and its border at every A-check for the first 2 000 flight hours, then at every C-check. A disbond found at the repair boundary invalidates the repair. Record the repair against the fairing serial number, not against the aircraft, because fairings are rotated between aircraft.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Damage up to 90 mm across in the skin only, not reaching a fastener line, not extending into a bonded edge member, and no more than two existing scarf repairs on the same fairing.

type_data.fastener_pattern: Not applicable; the repair is bonded. The fairing is re-installed on its standard fastener pattern.
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Not life limited. Tap test of the repair and a 100 mm border at every A-check for the first 2 000 flight hours, then at every C-check.

issue.reason: A maximum cavity soak temperature is stated for the repaired laminate, replacing the case-by-case answer given when a fairing was moved to a ventilated heat shield aircraft.

On aircraft that have the ventilated heat shield, check the standoff dimension at every boss inside the repair area after the first ground run, because the repaired laminate is locally thicker and the shield sits on it.
